nodes.label: Media over QUIC Transport (Draft 14)
nodes.author: S. Nandakumar, V. Vasiliev, I. Swett, A. Frindell

nodes.label: SRT Live Ingest to MoQ Publishing Technical Note
nodes.norm_label: srt live ingest to moq publishing technical note

nodes.label: openmoq_publisher_lib Static Library
nodes.rationale: Shipped as a reusable static archive (libopenmoq_publisher.a / openmoq_publisher.lib) so external projects can embed the publisher; CMake consumers link the target to inherit include paths, C++20 requirement, and transport dependencies (picoquic, picotls, OpenSSL, platform sockets).

nodes.label: CTE LL-DASH Ingest Mode
nodes.rationale: Adds CTE LL-DASH as a live publishing mechanism by accepting multiple concurrent HTTP/1.1 chunked CMAF ingest paths; deliberately reuses StreamingMp4Reader, track extraction, live catalog/fragment builders, and Publisher::publish_live_objects so the new surface stays limited to one live ingest module plus CLI wiring.

nodes.label: PreparedPublish
nodes.rationale: Separates prepare (input_bytes + plan) from publish so larger apps can inspect/approve plan output, store plan state, and publish the same prepared asset to multiple endpoints.

nodes.label: Publisher::publish_live
nodes.rationale: Default live path: consumes one fragmented MP4 byte stream (ftyp/moov then moof/mdat pairs) with incremental parsing instead of buffering to EOF, matching ffmpeg/CMAF pipelines.

nodes.label: Publisher::publish_live_objects
nodes.rationale: Bypasses fragmented MP4 ingest for applications that already produce MoQ objects directly; each LiveObject supplies track, group/object IDs, optional media timing, and payload bytes.

nodes.label: Publisher::stats Publish Summary
nodes.rationale: Because the publisher API is blocking with no built-in polling loop, stats are exposed as a structured summary of the current/last publish rather than a live telemetry stream; stats() is thread-safe to poll from a GUI thread while publish blocks a worker. stats_json() is deprecated because a JSON polling API implies runtime telemetry support the blocking API does not provide.

nodes.label: shutdown() Does Not Wake accept() on macOS/BSD
nodes.rationale: Root cause: on Linux, shutdown(listen_fd, SHUT_RDWR) on a listening socket wakes a blocked accept() with EINVAL; on macOS/BSD shutdown() on a listening (unconnected) socket fails with ENOTCONN and does NOT wake accept(). Commit 6c08575 deferred close() until after the accept thread joins (fixing an fd-reuse race) but relied on shutdown() as the wake mechanism, which is Linux-only behavior; historically close() woke accept() on BSD, so the hang only appeared once close was deferred.
nodes.norm_label: shutdown() does not wake accept() on macos/bsd

nodes.label: macOS CI Hang in openmoq-publisher-live-dash-tests
nodes.rationale: Symptom: macOS CI (build-and-test macos-latest) took ~26 minutes on every push to feature/ctedash; the openmoq-publisher-live-dash-tests binary hung in the first server start/stop test until ctest killed it at the 1500 s per-test timeout (exit code 8). Linux and Windows were unaffected. After fix commit 65c5a4f, macOS CI run 28627497050 passed in 43 seconds.

nodes.label: Bounded poll() Accept Loop
nodes.rationale: Fix mechanism 1 (commit 65c5a4f, src/live_dash_ingest.cpp): the accept loop never parks in accept(); it waits in poll() on the listening fd with a bounded 100 ms timeout and re-checks stop_requested each cycle, mirroring the client workers' SO_RCVTIMEO receive cadence, so stop() never depends on shutdown() waking accept().

nodes.label: Non-Blocking Listening Socket
nodes.rationale: Fix mechanism 2: the listening socket is set O_NONBLOCK after listen(), so a connection aborted between the poll() wakeup and the accept() call cannot re-block the loop.

nodes.label: Clear Inherited O_NONBLOCK on Accepted Client fd
nodes.rationale: Fix mechanism 3: handle_client() clears O_NONBLOCK on the accepted client fd before applying SO_RCVTIMEO. BSD-derived systems (macOS) make accepted sockets inherit the listener's O_NONBLOCK while Linux does not; without clearing it the worker recv loop would hot-spin on EAGAIN instead of honoring the timed cadence.
nodes.norm_label: clear inherited o_nonblock on accepted client fd

nodes.label: Portable Listener Shutdown Rules
nodes.rationale: Rules: (1) never rely on shutdown() of a listening socket to unblock accept() - it is Linux-only; use a bounded poll()+stop-flag loop, a self-pipe, or a wake connection; (2) accepted sockets inherit O_NONBLOCK from the listener on BSD/macOS but not Linux - normalize the flag explicitly; (3) keeping a listening fd open until its accept thread joins avoids fd-reuse races, but then the wake mechanism must be something other than close().

nodes.label: SO_RCVTIMEO Receive Polling Cadence
nodes.rationale: Earlier partial fix (commit 8b4b99b) made client recv() responsive during shutdown via SO_RCVTIMEO polling, but did not touch accept(), so the listener hang persisted until 65c5a4f.

nodes.label: Fragmented MP4 (CMAF) Input Fast Path
nodes.rationale: The publisher's preferred fast path is already-fragmented MP4 (frag_keyframe+empty_moov+default_base_moof+separate_moof); progressive MP4 can be remuxed internally but pre-fragmented input is simpler and more efficient.

nodes.label: +separate_moof Track-Separated Fragments
nodes.rationale: The live path expects each moof+mdat pair to belong to a single media track; without +separate_moof audio and video may share one moof, which the current live parser does not accept - symptom is audio appearing in the catalog while no audio media objects are sent.

nodes.label: HEVC hev1-to-hvc1 Normalization
nodes.rationale: If a source is tagged hev1 but keeps VPS/SPS/PPS only in the init segment, the publisher normalizes the advertised codec and emitted init segment to hvc1; if HEVC samples carry in-band parameter sets, hev1 is preserved.

nodes.label: MOQT Draft-14 Primary Profile
nodes.rationale: Primary publisher profile: dedicated SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE_OK/ERROR and PUBLISH_NAMESPACE_OK/ERROR flows, NAMESPACE_PREFIX_OVERLAP handling, u16 outer Length on control messages with only (i)-marked inner fields as QUIC varints.

nodes.label: MOQT Draft-16 Compatibility Profile
nodes.rationale: Secondary compatibility target: generic REQUEST_OK/REQUEST_ERROR flow, Subscribe Options carried before message parameters in SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, delta-encoded key-value message parameters, and PUBLISH_OK defaults FORWARD=1 and SUBSCRIBER_PRIORITY=128 when parameters are omitted.

nodes.label: CMAF-to-MOQT Packaging Model
nodes.rationale: Init data is a binary payload or a dedicated MOQT track with one group/one object; media objects follow the styp?+moof+mdat fast path reusing boxes directly from fragmented MP4; one media object per fragment/group aligns with the fragment-to-group mapping in the current MOQT CMAF packaging draft.

nodes.label: Packaging / Control-Plane / Transport Layer Separation
nodes.rationale: The code intentionally separates MP4/CMAF packaging, draft-version control-plane mapping, and transport publication so the packaging path can be contributed first and a concrete OpenMOQ transport session wired in afterwards.

nodes.label: --forward 0/1 Publish Semantics
nodes.rationale: --forward 0 waits for inbound SUBSCRIBE before sending matching media objects (subscribers subscribe to catalog for discovery; --publish-catalog proactively publishes only the catalog track); --forward 1 proactively publishes tracks and objects after namespace setup, making it the right smoke-test mode. Time-aligned multitrack objects are served in publish-plan order to keep A/V interleaved.

nodes.label: TLS SNI Override (--sni)
nodes.rationale: Allows connecting to a relay by raw IP while presenting the relay hostname in TLS SNI; --insecure is reserved for intentionally untrusted certs so certificate/SNI regressions on public relays stay visible.

nodes.label: SRT MPEG-TS Ingest Pipeline
nodes.rationale: SRT 1316-byte datagrams -> buffered MPEG-TS -> 188-byte packets (sync 0x47) -> PAT/PMT/PES -> EsSample access units -> Annex-B/ADTS conversion -> synthesized moof+mdat per sample -> MoQ object. Unlike the stdin fMP4 path where ffmpeg creates moof+mdat and moqxr forwards as-is, the SRT path builds everything from scratch at true CMAF per-sample granularity (exactly one frame or one AAC access unit per MoQ object).

nodes.label: MediaFragment
nodes.rationale: Defined in cmaf_segmenter.h: group_id, object_id, track_name, timing, keyframe flag, and payload whose owned_bytes (raw moof+mdat) become the MoQ object payload sent as-is; the FragmentSink callback pushes each MediaFragment into a shared queue drained by the MoQ session's drain_queue loop.

nodes.label: Accumulation-Based tfdt Timing Model
nodes.rationale: base_decode_time is accumulation-based (each sample's tfdt = previous tfdt + previous sample_duration) rather than PTS-derived, guaranteeing strict monotonicity regardless of PTS jitter from SRT transport and preventing MSE 'overlapping payload' drops on the player. Audio duration is fixed at 1024 in the audio timescale; video duration comes from PTS deltas.

nodes.label: SRT Codec Discovery Phase
nodes.rationale: Before streaming, waits up to 5 seconds for the first video frame (codec type), first video keyframe (SPS/PPS/VPS -> avcC/hvcC), and first ADTS frame (esds); tracks without codec_private are removed, the init segment is rebuilt with real parameters, and the catalog is published as MoQ object group=0/object=0 on the catalog track.

nodes.label: Native QUIC vs WebTransport Connection Split
nodes.rationale: Two non-interchangeable connection models: native QUIC MoQ identifies the draft via QUIC ALPN and carries authority/path in MoQ SETUP; MoQ-over-WebTransport uses ALPN h3, HTTPS extended CONNECT with authority/path identifying the session, negotiates the MoQ version after CONNECT, and must NOT include AUTHORITY/PATH in MoQ SETUP.
nodes.norm_label: native quic vs webtransport connection split

nodes.label: WT-Available-Protocols / WT-Protocol Negotiation
nodes.rationale: MoQ-over-WebTransport draft selection is not QUIC ALPN; the MoQ application protocol identifier travels as HTTP Structured Fields strings on CONNECT (send "moqt-16" quoted, not bare). Draft-14 offers no subprotocol for legacy compatibility; drafts 16/17/18 offer moqt-16/17/18. Red5's picoquic/h3zero path no longer exposes WT-Available-Protocols on accept, so accepting without WT-Protocol is an interop compatibility mode, not proof CONNECT-level selection works.

nodes.label: WebTransport App-Stream Preamble (0x41 + Session ID)
nodes.rationale: Each WT bidi application stream begins with signal 0x41 plus a Session ID varint before application payload; the CONNECT stream carries capsule traffic and is not the MoQ control stream, so bytes on it must never be parsed as MoQ. picoquic helpers (picowt_prepare_client_cnx, picowt_set_control_stream, picowt_connect, picowt_create_local_stream) already cover this surface and should not be manually reproduced without a verified picoquic bug.

nodes.label: Idle Subscriber Timeout Behavior
nodes.rationale: With --forward 0, after PUBLISH_NAMESPACE_OK the publisher waits up to --timeout seconds for SUBSCRIBE; no subscriber means the session is treated as idle, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE_DONE is emitted, and the run exits successfully - intentional so interoperability probes are not reported as publish failures when the relay accepted the namespace but no subscriber appeared.

nodes.label: CTE DASH Ingest Dry-Run (--dump-plan)
nodes.rationale: --dump-plan with --live-source dash replaces the otherwise required --endpoint: the publisher starts the chunked-transfer ingest listener, waits for tracks, and prints the live plan instead of publishing to a relay; the dry run drains objects until interrupted, so scripted checks wrap it in timeout.

nodes.label: MOQT Draft Support (14/16/18)
nodes.rationale: Draft 14 is the primary target, draft 16 is maintained as a compatibility profile, and draft 18 support covers version selection, setup/request framing codec paths, and request-stream response correlation while interop hardening continues.

nodes.label: CTE LL-DASH/CMAF Live Ingest
nodes.rationale: Accepts live CTE LL-DASH/CMAF ingest over HTTP/1.1 chunked POST or PUT requests (--live-source dash); multiple concurrent paths under a prefix get path-prefixed track names in the MoQ catalog. Currently supported on Unix-like platforms only; Windows builds report the mode as unsupported.

nodes.label: SRT MPEG-TS Live Ingest
nodes.rationale: --live-source srt receives MPEG-TS over SRT (caller/listener config in a JSON file) and re-fragments to CMAF with keyframe-aligned fragments.

nodes.label: stdin Fragmented-MP4 Live Ingest
nodes.rationale: --live-source stdin pipes fragmented MP4 (frag_keyframe+empty_moov+default_base_moof+separate_moof) from ffmpeg directly into the publisher. --live-source both is intentionally not supported.

nodes.label: Draft-Aware MOQT Publish Plan
nodes.rationale: Turns MP4 input into CMSF-style publishable objects with catalog, optional MSF media timeline and SAP event timeline metadata; plans can be inspected locally (--dump-plan, --emit-dir) or published over picoquic-backed Raw QUIC and WebTransport. --forward 1 sends objects immediately, --forward 0 is await-subscribe mode.

nodes.label: CTest Unit Test Suite
nodes.rationale: Ten test executables (packaging, cli, srt-config, live-dash, transport, webtransport, publisher-api, cat4moq-api, cat4moq-transport-token, control-messages) all link openmoq_publisher_lib; picoquic loopback smoke tests are opt-in via OPENMOQ_RUN_PICOQUIC_SMOKE_TESTS.

nodes.label: picoquic Transport Dependency
nodes.rationale: Optional (OPENMOQ_ENABLE_PICOQUIC); consumed as an add_subdirectory source checkout defaulting to third_party/picoquic. On Linux with CMake >= 3.24 a LINK_GROUP:RESCAN resolves circular deps between picohttp-core, picoquic-log and picoquic-core; macOS/Windows link picoquic-core plus picohttp-core directly.

nodes.label: picotls TLS Dependency
nodes.rationale: Fetched by picoquic via PICOQUIC_FETCH_PTLS with FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_PICOTLS pinned to a local checkout. picotls declares CMake 2.8 compatibility so CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM 3.5 is forced. On Windows its POSIX-only cli/bench/test executables are excluded, wintimeofday.c is added to picotls-core, and picotls-minicrypto links bcrypt.

nodes.label: picotls Link-Directory Sanitization Workaround
nodes.rationale: picotls injects literal '(' and ')' link-directory entries when Brotli is discovered via pkg-config; after CMake normalization these become malformed source-prefixed paths that macOS CMake rejects during generate. Two-layer fix: PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR/PATH are scoped to an empty directory while picotls configures, and openmoq_sanitize_target_link_directories filters residual raw and normalized '('/')' entries from picotls-core.

nodes.label: Optional libsrt Ingest Support
nodes.rationale: OPENMOQ_ENABLE_SRT probes for srt/srt.h and libsrt; when found OPENMOQ_HAS_SRT=1 is defined on the publisher library, otherwise the build proceeds without SRT ingest runtime.

nodes.label: build-and-test CI Matrix
nodes.rationale: Single build-and-test job fanned out over ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, and windows-latest with fail-fast disabled so one platform failure does not cancel the others. Runs on push to main/master and on pull requests.

nodes.label: CI build-and-test (macos-latest)
nodes.rationale: macOS is the platform where picotls's malformed pkg-config link directories break CMake generate (worked around in CMakeLists.txt). This job recently hung on a DASH ingest test timeout during ctest, making it the sensitive leg of the matrix for the live DASH ingest tests.

nodes.label: CI build-and-test (windows-latest)
nodes.rationale: Requires extra setup: pkgconfiglite is installed because picotls requires pkg-config at configure time even though Brotli is absent on Windows, and OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR is discovered from known install paths or installed via choco. Tests run with -C Debug and the library is verified at build/Debug/openmoq_publisher.lib.

nodes.label: CI picoquic Source Checkout Step
nodes.rationale: Checks out private-octopus/picoquic at master into third_party/picoquic and passes it to CMake via -DOPENMOQ_PICOQUIC_SOURCE_DIR.

nodes.label: CI picotls Source Checkout Step
nodes.rationale: Checks out private-octopus/picotls at master with recursive submodules into third_party/picotls and passes it to CMake via -DOPENMOQ_PICOTLS_SOURCE_DIR.

nodes.label: CI ctest Test Step
nodes.rationale: Runs ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure (with -C Debug on Windows), executing every registered unit test on all three matrix platforms.

nodes.label: Release Builds Workflow (release.yml)
nodes.rationale: Triggered by v* tags or manual dispatch; builds Release-config binaries on the same three-OS matrix as CI, packages an SDK archive per platform, uploads workflow artifacts, and attaches assets to a GitHub release when the version starts with v.

nodes.label: Release Static-Library SDK Packaging
nodes.rationale: Stages libopenmoq_publisher plus its picoquic/picotls/picohttp transitive static libraries (whose symbols are otherwise undefined in the publisher archive) alongside headers, README, LICENSE and docs; OpenSSL stays a system dependency. Deps are located recursively because the build tree layout differs by generator (single-config Linux/macOS vs Release/ subdir on MSVC). The release fails if fewer than 5 libs are staged, rather than shipping an SDK that cannot link.

nodes.label: CAT4MOQ Authorization
nodes.rationale: CAT4MOQ uses CAT (CWT) tokens; the CWT moqt claim scopes allowed actions, namespace matches, and track-name matches, and all actions are blocked when a token is present unless explicitly enabled by a matching moqt scope. Publisher-relevant action keys: CLIENT_SETUP=0, ANNOUNCE=2, PUBLISH=6. WebTransport carries tokens in CAT/CAT1/CAT2 query params or CAT-/CAT1-/CAT2- path components; native QUIC uses the PATH setup parameter; per-action authorization uses the MoQ authorization token parameter on request messages.

nodes.label: MoQ AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN Wrapping
nodes.rationale: Raw Catapult CWT bytes are wrapped as USE_VALUE alias mode (0x03) plus token type (CAT=0x10/16, out-of-band=0x00) plus CWT bytes. The relay's auth.token_type must match the wrapper (cat -> 16, out-of-band -> 0, none -> token source already contains the full encoded value). Token input decoding defaults to auto: binary raw, base64: prefix, hex:/0x prefix, or plain text.

nodes.label: Catapult CAT4MOQ Token Issuer
nodes.rationale: Tokens come from a file (CAT4MOQ_TOKEN_FILE or separate setup/action files) or from CATAPULT_CAT4MOQ_COMMAND, a command printing a token to stdout with shell-quoted {action}/{namespace}/{track}/{endpoint} placeholders. The sibling moqx relay can act as issuer via moqx issue-cat-token, printing base64:<token> by default.

nodes.label: moqx Sibling Relay
nodes.rationale: The sibling moqx relay hosts the existing Catapult/CAT4MOQ verifier logic; the example deliberately does not implement relay-side validation. Local config enables auth with token_type 16, HMAC keys, require_setup_token and allow_request_token_override.

nodes.label: Public API Boundary for Auth Types
nodes.rationale: Any reusable auth, CAT, CAT4MOQ, action-scope, token-carriage, or token-wrapper concept needed by applications must live in public API headers under include/openmoq/publisher (cat4moq::Action, AuthorizationToken, AuthorizationConfig, wrap_cat_token, PublisherConfig::authorization); transport internals consume those API types, and examples/auth may only contain executable orchestration and Catapult command wiring. This keeps AuthPublisher.cpp free of transport headers while configured tokens still reach setup and request message encoders.
nodes.norm_label: public api boundary for auth types
